title: PSEi rallies 2.22% ahead of MSCI rebalancing; peso weakens
summary: Philippine financial markets ended mixed on Friday, with the peso weakening slightly against the US dollar while the local stock market rallied 2.22% as investors positioned themselves ahead of the…
byline: JON VIKTOR D. CABUENAS, GMA News

blocks.text: Philippine financial markets ended mixed on Friday, with the peso weakening slightly against the US dollar while the local stock market rallied 2.22% as investors positioned themselves ahead of the MSCI index rebalancing.
The local currency shed a centavo to close Friday at P63.73:$1 from Thursday’s finish of P63.72:$1.

“The US dollar/peso exchange rate again corrected slightly higher after record high exports on a monthly basis, especially electronics due to strong artificial intelligence (AI) demand, but offset by record imports and trade deficit on a monthly basis,” Rizal Commercial Banking Corp. (RCBC) chief economist Michael Ricafort said in a mobile message.

Preliminary data released by the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) showed that the country’s trade deficit widened to a record $6.953 billion in October, the highest level since the government started compiling merchandise trade statistics in 1991.
Exports stood at $10.565 billion, also the highest since data collection began in 1991. The largest jump was seen in the export of electronic products, which grew by $3.206 billion.

Ricafort also cited BSP Governor Eli Remolona Jr.’s remarks earlier this week, saying a pause in monetary policy tightening is possible but unlikely, while maintaining that prolonged economic weakness may have weakened the case for aggressive rate hikes.
The Philippine Stock Exchange index (PSEi), meanwhile, gained 121.84 points or 2.22% to 5,611.97. The broader All Shares grew by 42.51 points or 2.39% to 3,095.48.
All sectoral indices closed higher — financials by 0.98%, industrial by 1.21%, holding firms by 0.44%, property by 0.33%, services by 5.42%, and mining and oil by 3.01%.
More than 1.722 billion shares, valued at P29.167 billion, changed hands. Advancers led decliners, 81 to 79, and 75 issues were unchanged.

“I think the primary reason would be more of the positioning on the MSCI rebalancing. So, that really, I think ‘yan ‘yung (that is the) primary factor,” First Grade Finance managing director Astro del Castillo said in a phone interview.
“Technically, it's really oversold. It's really due for a bounce,” he said.

Friday’s session was the last session before the implementation of the MSCI’s November index changes, as there will be no trading on Monday, November 30, in commemoration of Bonifacio Day, which was earlier declared a regular holiday. –NB, GMA News
